question.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of hedge funds as described in SEBI's definition?

answer.text: They invest only in government securities
They employ diverse or complex trading strategies and invest in securities having diverse risks or complex products
They cannot use leverage at fund level
They focus exclusively on real estate investments

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI defines a hedge fund as an AIF that employs diverse or complex trading strategies and invests or trades in securities having diverse risks or complex products, including listed and unlisted derivatives. Hedge funds sit within Category III, which is the category permitted to use leverage at fund level. The Trap: Government-securities-only and real-estate-only mandates do not match the SEBI definition. The 'cannot use leverage at fund level' option is the opposite of the Category III treatment. Note: Use only the workbook-supported definitional language and the Category III/leverage contrast; avoid adding directives or distributor-certification advice that is not in the cited pages.
